quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Your kayak capsizes in calm lake water during a practice paddle. After performing a wet exit, what is your immediate priority in the water?
options: Abandon the kayak and paddle and try to swim 300 yards to the nearest shoreline.
Maintain physical contact with your capsized kayak and paddle, signal your buddy boat, and position yourself at the bow/stern for a T-rescue or heel-hook re-entry.
Unbuckle and remove your PFD life jacket so you can swim faster.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Hold onto your kayak and paddle, keep your PFD fastened, and coordinate a buddy T-rescue.
quiz_item.explanation: A swamped kayak provides massive flotation and high visibility for rescuers, whereas swimming away in open water risks cold-water exhaustion and separation.

pamphlet_excerpts: Selecting Kayak Paddle: In selecting a kayak paddle, the most important thing toconsider is the comfort of the paddle in your hands.
Qualitypaddles Oval Shaft: Qualitypaddles have an oval shaft, which provides better control andcomfort and helps you set the correct angle.
Paddles Havestraight Shafts: Most paddles havestraight shafts, but a few designs are bent at the grip positionsto ease strain on the wrists.
Paddlesfor Recreational: Paddlesfor recreational kayaks are normally sized in centimeters, withtypical lengths between 200 and 220 centimeters.
step_by_step_procedure: Given Differences General: Given these differences, a general rule of thumb for sizing akayak paddle is to hold the paddle above your head horizontally.
Elbows Degree Angles: With your elbows at 90-degree angles, your hands should be 6 to 8 inches from the throat on either end of the paddle.
Blades Kayak Paddles: The blades of kayak paddles come in various designs.
Largeblades Provide Power: Largeblades provide more power per stroke; smaller blades take lessenergy per stroke and are gentler to arm and shoulder joints.

requirements.req_text: As a solo paddler, use a properly equipped kayak to demonstrate the following: (a) Paddle a straight line for 15 to 20 boat lengths using appropriate strokes while maintaining trim and balance of the kayak. (b) Spin or pivot from a stationary position 180 degrees (half circle) to the right and left within two boat lengths. (c) Move abeam to the right 10 feet and to the left 10 feet. (d) Stop the boat in one boat length. (e) While maintaining forward motion, turn the kayak 90 degrees to the right and left. (f) Move the kayak backward three to four boat lengths using appropriate and effective reverse strokes. (g) Paddle the kayak in a buoyed figure 8 course around markers three to four boat lengths apart.

Paddleblade Water Beplaced: When the paddleblade is put in the water, it should beplaced in a way so the boat moves inthe direction you want to go.
Ideally Energy Applied: Ideally, all the energy applied to thepaddle should make the boat go wherethe paddler wants.
Happen Anchor Few: For this to happen, it helps to anchor a few things in place.
step_by_step_procedure: Paddler Anchorhimself Boat: First, the paddler needs to anchorhimself in the boat.
Outfittinghelps Does Gently: Good outfittinghelps, as does gently pushing with thefeet, legs, and buttocks during eachpaddle stroke.
Paddle Needsto Well-anchored: Second, the paddle needsto be well-anchored to the paddler.
Asolid Grip Strong: Asolid grip and a strong arm positionhelp transmit the paddle’s power fromthe water through the paddler’s bodyto the boat.
